body: No need to add new menu. The items are re-created every time.
The order of method definitions in cpp file should match the order of declarations (currently it doesn't).

If it's not too complicated, you could instead disable the menu item if the node is invalid.

EDIT:
Also technically referring to "node" is incorrect, as the target can be any Object.
It would be nice to get rid of this connecting/disconnecting logic. You can carry the information about selected track by using a new variable (or reusing one from the existing dialogs).

I've disabled the menu when the node is invalid (and also when the track type does not support properties). This error message might be redundant as a result.

>Also technically referring to "node" is incorrect, as the target can be any Object.

I could be missing an edge case, but I imagine this refers to when pointing to an object referenced by a node like `Node3D/Sprite3D:material_override:shader` references a material_override object, and the shader within that object.

This particular error message checks for the node in the path (In this case Sprite3D the child of Node3D) without regard to the properties. It _sounds_ correct to me but let me know if I'm missing something.
